references.text: The blood was to be applied to the doorposts and the upper lintel, as preparation for the sign described in verse 13.
The Lord will pass over the doorway and not allow the destroyer to enter the houses when he sees the blood on the lintel and the doorposts.
Fulfillment of judgment against Egypt—all firstborn in Egypt were struck down, while Israel was spared because of the blood.
The blood serves as atonement for the soul, a principle underlying the protective power of the Passover lamb's blood.
The Lord will 'pass over' (פָּסַח) and spare Jerusalem, using the same Hebrew word that refers to Passover.
A sign on the forehead protects the righteous from destruction, parallel to the blood as a sign on the doors.
Πίστει πεποίηκεν τὸ πάσχα καὶ τὴν πρόσχυσιν τοῦ αἵματος - By faith Moses kept the Passover and applied the blood, so that the destroyer did not touch the firstborn.
Believers are chosen to be cleansed by the blood of Jesus Christ (ῥαντισμὸν αἵματος Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ), which fulfills the meaning of the Passover lamb's blood.
God's servants are sealed on their foreheads before destruction comes, parallel to the blood as a sign for protection.
Christ, our Passover lamb (τὸ πάσχα ἡμῶν ἐτύθη Χριστός), has been sacrificed—his blood is the ultimate fulfillment of the Passover lamb's blood.
Both use 'sign' centrally in the Exodus account: the blood as a sign of deliverance and the law as a sign of remembrance.
Causal connection: God's plan to strike Egypt (cause) makes the sign of the blood necessary for salvation (effect).
Theological parallel: The 'sign' in Egypt linked to God's act of salvation (historical blood versus prophetic Savior).
Theological contrast: God's eye that does not spare (judgment) versus God's eye that sees the blood and spares (grace).
The same theological contrast as 7: God's eye that brings judgment without sparing versus the sign of the blood that secures grace.
Continuity in God's covenant: The promise of protection and presence from the Exodus is confirmed by the prophet (Haggai).
